sources.title: workspace_write sandbox permission template
sources.product: Codex CLI workspace-write policy
claims_supported: Source directly describes or constrains the listed execution topologies
claims_not_supported: Does not prove that all process-creation paths, interpreters, hooks, inherited descriptors, or external effects traverse the same policy.

sources.title: Sandbox bypass due to bug in path configuration logic (GHSA-w5fx-fh39-j5rw, CVE-2025-59532)
sources.product: Codex CLI sandbox boundary validation advisory
claims_supported: Source directly describes or constrains the listed execution topologies
claims_not_supported: Does not prove current versions are bypassable, that all Codex versions are unsafe, or that one historical path bug defeats the whole execution architecture.
sources.limitations: Applies to affected versions `0.2.0–0.38.0`; advisory says fixed in `0.39.0`. It documents one path-configuration failure and explicitly notes that the network-disabled sandbox restriction was not impacted.

sources.title: Configure the sandboxed Bash tool
sources.product: Claude Code Bash sandbox; bubblewrap, Seatbelt, optional seccomp filter, filesystem/network restrictions, credential controls
claims_supported: Source directly describes or constrains the listed execution topologies
claims_not_supported: Does not establish coverage of all Claude Code tools, direct host process creation outside the command surface, ET-02, all hooks/configuration paths, or complete mediation.
sources.limitations: The documented boundary is commands run through Bash/PowerShell/Monitor and their child processes. Native Windows is not supported; unsupported/missing dependencies warn and run unsandboxed by default unless `sandbox.failIfUnavailable=true`; an unsandboxed retry escape hatch exists unless disabled.

sources.title: Configure permissions
sources.product: Claude Code tool permission rules, modes, hooks, and working-directory policy
claims_supported: Source directly describes or constrains the listed execution topologies
claims_not_supported: Does not convert approval/permission rules into host-wide OS mediation or prove ET-01/ET-02/ET-03/ET-05/ET-06/ET-10 coverage.
sources.limitations: Permission rules are enforced by Claude Code, while sandboxing is a separate layer; command-text matching has documented alternate-invocation limitations. `bypassPermissions` is intended only for isolated environments.

sources.title: Sandbox escape via symlink following allows arbitrary file write outside workspace (GHSA-vp62-r36r-9xqp, CVE-2026-39861)
sources.product: Claude Code sandbox path/symlink boundary advisory
claims_supported: Source directly describes or constrains the listed execution topologies
claims_not_supported: Does not prove the current patched version is vulnerable, that Claude Code is generally unsafe, or that this one issue demonstrates universal topology bypass.
sources.limitations: Advisory is version-scoped (`<2.1.64` affected; `2.1.64` patched) and describes a composition failure between sandboxed symlink creation and an unsandboxed write path.

sources.title: Sandboxing in Gemini CLI
sources.product: Gemini CLI sandbox providers: Docker/Podman, macOS Seatbelt, Windows native, gVisor/runsc, LXC/LXD, tool-level sandboxing
claims_supported: Source directly describes or constrains the listed execution topologies
claims_not_supported: Does not prove that every Gemini CLI tool or process path is inside one common enforcement boundary, nor ET-01/ET-02/ET-07/ET-09/ET-11/ET-12 complete coverage or complete mediation.
sources.limitations: Provider and platform behavior differ. Sandboxing is opt-in in normal configuration; workspace bind mounts, network allowance, sandbox expansion, custom flags, Docker socket sharing, and pre-existing LXC requirements materially change the boundary.

sources.title: Policy engine reference
sources.product: Gemini CLI tool-call policy engine (allow, deny, ask_user)
claims_supported: Source directly describes or constrains the listed execution topologies
claims_not_supported: Does not prove process-level or kernel-level mediation, argument/path completeness, resistance to alternate process paths, or universal host governance.
sources.limitations: Policy decisions are tool-call decisions; in non-interactive mode `ask_user` is treated as deny. This is distinct from the underlying OS/container sandbox.

sources.title: Run Modes — local agent approvals and sandboxing
sources.product: Cursor local Agent; Auto-review/Allowlist/Run Everything, shell sandbox, macOS Seatbelt, Linux Landlock/bubblewrap
claims_supported: Source directly describes or constrains the listed execution topologies
claims_not_supported: Does not prove ET-01/ET-02/ET-09/ET-11/ET-12/ET-13 coverage for all agent surfaces, nor complete mediation or current behavior on every platform.
sources.limitations: The page limits the claim to local shell commands and says unsupported/full-system commands can run outside the sandbox with approval. SDK/local defaults and Cloud Agent behavior are separate. Network defaults and fallback backend are configurable.

sources.title: Security overview — Cloud Agents
sources.product: Cursor Cloud Agents; per-agent VM boundary, network egress, runtime secrets, file exclusion, draft-PR workflow
claims_supported: Source directly describes or constrains the listed execution topologies
claims_not_supported: Does not prove host-wide mediation, local-agent mediation, kernel hook coverage, or that VM isolation covers every external effect.
sources.limitations: Describes a cloud-agent VM and service controls, not the local Cursor CLI/desktop shell boundary. Internet access is on by default unless restricted; scope is bounded by repository/user/tool configuration.

sources.title: Cursor TypeScript SDK — sandbox options
sources.product: Cursor local/headless SDK agent
claims_supported: Source directly describes or constrains the listed execution topologies
claims_not_supported: Does not prove mediation of non-shell SDK operations, ET-01/ET-02/ET-07/ET-09/ET-10/ET-12/ET-13, or complete mediation.
sources.limitations: Local SDK sandbox is disabled by default; when enabled, shell tools and shell-spawned processes are constrained. Headless runs have no human approval callback, so classifier-blocked calls are denied.

sources.title: Runtime architecture
sources.product: OpenHands Docker Runtime; backend/client to action-execution server; shell, browser, plugins, Jupyter inside runtime container
claims_supported: Source directly describes or constrains the listed execution topologies
claims_not_supported: Does not prove all OpenHands execution surfaces use Docker, does not prove host-wide ET-01/ET-02/ET-07/ET-08/ET-09/ET-11/ET-13 mediation, and does not prove complete mediation.
sources.limitations: The documented Docker runtime is a deployment topology, with REST communication and a user-provided/custom image. The existence of a runtime boundary depends on deployment configuration.

sources.title: Docker Runtime (V0; legacy)
sources.product: OpenHands Docker sandbox, bind mounts, runtime user ID, network binding/isolation guidance
claims_supported: Source directly describes or constrains the listed execution topologies
claims_not_supported: Does not establish complete mediation, immutable workspace protection, host escape resistance, or coverage of non-Docker/local runtime paths.
sources.limitations: Explicitly labeled legacy V0. Mounted files are writable/deletable by the agent; default network binding can expose interfaces; hardening requires operator configuration.

sources.title: Landlock: unprivileged access control
sources.product: Landlock LSM; self-applied, stackable filesystem/network/IPC restrictions inherited by future children
claims_supported: Source directly describes or constrains the listed execution topologies
claims_not_supported: Does not prove ET-02 or universal indirect-path coverage, identity/PDP binding, policy revocation, or complete mediation of an Agent CLI.
sources.limitations: Landlock restricts only handled rights and supported ABI features; availability/ABI must be checked at runtime. It is self-restriction, not a general host-wide policy service. Documented special-filesystem and topology limitations remain.

sources.title: Landlock: system-wide management
sources.product: Landlock audit and trace events
claims_supported: Source directly describes or constrains the listed execution topologies
claims_not_supported: Does not prove that an audit record exists for every execution path or that auditability equals complete mediation.
sources.limitations: Audit/trace visibility depends on audit configuration and privileged access to trace events; observability is not itself authorization.

sources.title: AppArmor
sources.product: AppArmor task-centered MAC profiles
claims_supported: Source directly describes or constrains the listed execution topologies
claims_not_supported: Does not prove a profile exists, is attached to the intended Agent identity, covers every alternate path, fails closed on policy failure, or establishes complete mediation.
sources.limitations: The kernel documentation states that tasks without a loaded profile are unconfined and that restrictions require a user-space-loaded policy. Module presence is not enforcement evidence.

sources.title: Linux Security Modules: General Security Hooks
sources.product: LSM framework and hook infrastructure
claims_supported: Source directly describes or constrains the listed execution topologies
claims_not_supported: Does not support a claim that “LSM enabled” means a policy is enforcing, nor a complete-mediation claim without module-specific evidence.
sources.limitations: The framework provides hooks/infrastructure but, by itself, adds no security; an enforcing module and loaded policy are required.

sources.title: LSM BPF Programs
sources.product: eBPF programs attached to LSM hooks for MAC/audit policies
claims_supported: Source directly describes or constrains the listed execution topologies
claims_not_supported: Does not prove BPF-LSM is active on a host, that `execve`/`execveat` and all alternate paths are hooked, or that a BPF program provides complete mediation.
sources.limitations: Loading/attachment requires privileged control and a verifier-accepted program. The document demonstrates hook attachment and detach, not a particular policy, identity model, lifecycle, or all execution hooks.

sources.title: Seccomp BPF
sources.product: Seccomp syscall filtering, inheritance, user notification
claims_supported: Source directly describes or constrains the listed execution topologies
claims_not_supported: Does not support filesystem/path/identity semantics by itself, arbitrary command authorization, ET-02 complete coverage, or complete mediation.
sources.limitations: The kernel documentation explicitly says syscall filtering is not a sandbox; filters inspect syscall number/arguments and cannot dereference pointers. Inheritance depends on allowed `fork`/`clone`/`execve`; installation requires `no_new_privs` or `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`.

sources.title: Linux Container Configuration
sources.product: OCI Linux container runtime; namespaces, cgroups, capabilities, LSM, filesystem jails, masked/readonly paths
claims_supported: Source directly describes or constrains the listed execution topologies
claims_not_supported: Does not prove a given container deployment is hardened, that the Docker/container API is itself mediated, or that container isolation is host-wide complete mediation.
sources.limitations: The specification defines configuration semantics; enforcement depends on the runtime, host kernel, privileges, mounts, selected namespaces, and policy. Omitted namespace types may be inherited from the runtime namespace.

sources.title: Integrity Policy Enforcement (IPE)
sources.product: IPE integrity policy enforcement
claims_supported: Source directly describes or constrains the listed execution topologies
claims_not_supported: Does not support generic command authorization, runtime identity/capability mediation, network/IPC governance, or complete mediation of Agent execution.
sources.limitations: IPE is an integrity-policy mechanism, not an inherent integrity verifier; the administrator chooses integrity providers. The documentation notes limitations for interpreted languages unless the interpreter uses `AT_EXECVE_CHECK`.

sources.title: A Note on the Confinement Problem
sources.product: Classical confinement and information-flow problem
execution_paths: Conceptual anchor for ET-08, ET-13, ET-14 and alternate-path analysis
claims_supported: Source directly describes or constrains the listed execution topologies
claims_not_supported: Does not prove that a named Agent CLI is confined/unconfined, nor that any sandbox is universally bypassable.
